en.name: Egusi (melon seeds)
en.summary: Egusi keeps 2–3 weeks in the cupboard, 3 months in the refrigerator and 9 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Those figures are read across from pine nuts, the oiliest seed with a published timeline — nothing is published for egusi itself.
en.pantry: 2–3 weeks at room temperature, and only for what you will use soon. Egusi is roughly half oil, which is why it thickens a stew so well and also why it turns: rancid egusi is bitter, and the smell is unmistakable once you know it. Take the range as guidance borrowed from pine nuts rather than as a published figure. Ground egusi has far more exposed surface than whole seed and goes off several times faster, so grind in small batches and keep the rest whole in a sealed jar, away from the hob and out of the sun.
en.fridge: 3 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, airtight and sealed hard — it takes up fridge smells as readily as any nut, and once it has, the flavour is in every stew you make with it. This is where a working quantity of egusi belongs in most kitchens, given how short the cupboard window is. Let the jar come back to room temperature before opening it, so condensation lands on the glass rather than on the seed.
en.freezer: 9 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is the right place for a big bag, whole or ground. There is very little water in egusi, so it does not go icy and does not clump; use it straight from the freezer without thawing. Portion it into several bags rather than one large one, so most of the batch stays frozen and sealed while you work through the rest.
en.thawing: No thawing is needed — use it straight from the freezer. If you do take a jar out, let it reach room temperature sealed before opening it.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp, paint-like smell — rancid egusi announces itself.
A bitter taste in a stew that should be rich and nutty.
Clumping or caking, meaning moisture has got in.
Mould, a musty smell, or insects in the jar.
tips: Grind only what you need; ground egusi ages several times faster than whole.
Keep the working jar in the fridge and the bulk in the freezer.
Smell it before you cook — rancidity carries straight into the dish.
Seal hard; egusi takes up fridge and freezer odours quickly.

faq.a: 2–3 weeks in the cupboard, 3 months refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 9 months frozen at −18 °C. Those figures are read across from pine nuts.
Yes, for anything beyond a few weeks. It is about half oil and goes rancid quickly at room temperature, especially once ground.

faq.q: How can you tell if egusi has gone bad?
faq.a: Smell it. Rancid egusi is sharply bitter and unmistakable, and the bitterness carries straight into the stew.

zh.name: 西非瓜籽（egusi）
zh.summary: Egusi 放櫥櫃 2～3 週、冷藏 3 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 9 個月。這組數字是比照松子（資料庫裡含油量最高、又有公布期限的種子）得來的——沒有任何資料是針對 egusi 本身的。
zh.pantry: 室溫 2～3 週，而且只適用於很快就會用掉的量。Egusi 大約有一半是油脂，這既是它能把燉菜勾得濃稠的原因，也是它會變質的原因：走油的 egusi 入口發苦，那個氣味你聞過一次就不會認錯。請把這個範圍當成向松子借來的參考，而不是公布的數字。磨成粉的 egusi 暴露面積遠大於整粒，變質速度快好幾倍，所以請少量現磨，其餘整粒密封放罐子裡，遠離爐台與陽光。
zh.fridge: 密封確實放 4 °C 以下，3 個月。它吸冰箱味道的本事和堅果一樣強，而一旦吸了，你之後煮的每一鍋湯都會帶上那個味道。考慮到櫥櫃那個很短的期限，日常用量放冰箱才是多數廚房的正解。罐子要等回到室溫再打開，讓水氣凝在玻璃上而不是種子上。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 9 個月；買一大包的話，不論整粒或磨粉，這裡就是它該待的地方。Egusi 含水量極低，不會結冰晶也不會結塊，可以直接從冷凍取用、不必解凍。請分裝成好幾個小袋而不是一大袋，這樣在你慢慢用的時候，大部分仍然維持冷凍與密封。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，直接從冷凍使用。若要把罐子拿出來，請密封著回到室溫再打開。
spoilage: 聞起來發苦、尖銳、像油漆——走油的 egusi 會自己招供。
本該濃郁堅果味的燉菜嚐起來發苦。
結塊、結成硬團，代表水氣跑進去了。
長霉、有霉味，或罐子裡有蟲。
tips: 要用多少磨多少，磨粉的老化速度是整粒的好幾倍。
日常用的小罐放冷藏，大量放冷凍。
下鍋前先聞一下，走油的味道會原封不動進到菜裡。
密封要確實，它吸冰箱與冷凍庫味道的速度很快。

faq.a: 櫥櫃 2～3 週、冷藏 4 °C 以下 3 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 9 個月。這組數字是比照松子得來的。
超過幾週的量就要。它大約一半是油脂，在室溫下走油很快，磨粉之後更快。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷 egusi 壞了？
faq.a: 用聞的。走油的 egusi 尖銳發苦，而且那股苦味會直接進到燉菜裡。
